questions.q: What does gap=5 do in TimeSeriesSplit?
options: Drops 5 rows between the end of training and the start of the test block
Makes the test set 5 rows long
why: n_splits sets the number of folds.

questions.q: Why is train_test_split(shuffle=True) wrong for time series?
options: Future rows enter the training set and neighbouring rows are similar, so the score is too optimistic

questions.q: TimeSeriesSplit(n_splits=3) on 12 rows with no gap. How many rows are in the first training set? (default test_size = n_samples // (n_splits + 1))
questions.why: test_size = 12 // 4 = 3. The last fold's test set is the last 3 rows, and training sets expand backwards from there: fold sizes 3, 6, 9. The first training set has 3 rows.

questions.q: Scenario: your target is the sum of the next 7 days, and you use TimeSeriesSplit with gap=0. Why is the CV score too good?
options: Targets of the last training rows overlap in time with the first test rows
why: Correct: use gap=6 or more so no training target overlaps the test period.

questions.q: Scenario: boosting does worse than Ridge on a strongly trending series. What is a good fix?
options: Predict the difference y[t] − y[t−1] and add it back
why: Correct: differencing makes the target stationary and inside the training range.
More trees do not allow extrapolation.
